title: Ideal ADC LSB voltage
description: Find the ideal code-bin width for an N-bit converter from its full-scale input span.
assumptions: Uniform ideal converter with 2^N code bins covering the specified full-scale span.
Full-scale span is the upper reference minus the lower reference, not the voltage of the highest reconstruction level.
Resolution does not establish accuracy; offset, gain, INL, DNL and noise are excluded.

references.title: Texas Instruments SLAA694A, General Oversampling of MSP ADCs for Higher Resolution, section 2.1, equation 1

constraints.message: Resolution must be an integer number of bits.

title: Ideal ADC code and quantization error
description: Quantize a specific input voltage using an explicitly defined uniform midrise transfer, then report its midpoint reconstruction and signed error.
formula: q = (V_high - V_low)/2^N; k = floor((V_in - V_low)/q); V_hat = V_low + (k + 1/2)q; error = (k + 1/2)q - (V_in - V_low) = V_hat - V_in
assumptions: Uniform midrise model: bin k is [V_low+kq, V_low+(k+1)q), reconstructed at its midpoint.
The input is inside the nonsaturated interval V_low <= V_in < V_high; the upper endpoint is excluded.
Unsigned straight-binary code labels are used even when the analog interval is bipolar.
This explicit midpoint convention is not a universal device transfer curve; consult device transition specifications. Offset, INL, DNL, noise and saturation behavior are excluded.

Signed error is evaluated in coordinates relative to the lower endpoint to avoid subtracting a rounded absolute reconstruction from the input. Absolute reconstruction can round to the endpoint/input when the bin is smaller than their binary64 spacing.

references.title: University of Texas at Austin EE445S, Lecture 8 Quantization notes, midrise quantization and error analysis
Texas Instruments ADCPro User Guide SBAU128C, appendix A.1.1 ADC transfer and quantization error

constraints.message: Resolution must be an integer number of bits.
The upper endpoint must exceed the lower endpoint by at least 1 nV.
Input must not lie below the nonsaturated converter interval.
Input must remain below full scale after floating-point normalization.
Input must be below the excluded upper endpoint.
